headline: Sotheby’s Sells “Jodi” the Nanotyrannus for $47.3 Million, Reigniting the Fossil Ownership Debate
summary: “Jodi” is now the second-most-valuable dinosaur ever sold at auction. The unexpected juxtaposition paid off: the skeleton sold for $5.4 million against a $2.5 million low estimate. The dinosaur auction record has climbed from $8.36 million for “Sue,” the Tyrannosaurus rex sold at Sotheby’s in 1997, to $31.85 million for “Stan” at Christie’s in 2020 and $50.13 million for “Gus” at Sotheby’s earlier this year—a sixfold increase.
